en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I am studying tonight.
tamil: நாளைக்கு எனக்கு பரீட்சை இருக்கு, அதனால இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி படிச்சிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend why you cannot go out.
explain: 'So' joins a reason with its result. 'Am studying' shows an action happening now.
usage: Use it with friends when you must refuse an invitation because of studies.
leelaQ: Do you study at night or in the morning?
answer: I study at night because the house is quiet.

en: When does your exam start?
tamil: உன் பரீட்சை எப்போ ஆரம்பிக்கும்?
context: Asking a friend about the exam date.
explain: A 'When' question asks for the time. The helper 'does' comes before the subject.
usage: Use it with a classmate when you plan your own preparation.
leelaQ: What is the first exam on your timetable?
answer: The first exam is English on Monday.

en: Our teacher explained the lesson very clearly.
tamil: எங்க டீச்சர் பாடத்தை ரொம்ப தெளிவா விளக்கினாங்க.
context: Praising a teacher to a classmate.
explain: 'Explained' is the past of explain. 'Very clearly' adds strength to the praise.
usage: Say it to classmates or parents when a teacher teaches well.
leelaQ: Who is your favourite teacher and why?
answer: My favourite teacher is my maths sir because he explains everything slowly.

en: Please open your books to page twenty.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு உங்க புத்தகத்தை இருபதாம் பக்கத்துல திறங்க.
explain: 'Please' makes an order polite. 'Open to page' is a classroom phrase.
usage: Teachers use it to start the lesson politely.
leelaQ: What do you say to start a class?
answer: I say good morning and ask everyone to open the book.

en: I will finish my homework before dinner.
tamil: நான் சாப்பாட்டுக்கு முன்னாடி என் ஹோம்வொர்க்கை முடிச்சிடுவேன்.
context: Promising a parent you will complete homework.
explain: 'Will' shows a promise about the future. 'Before dinner' gives the time limit.
usage: Use it with your mother or father when they ask about your homework.
leelaQ: When do you usually do your homework?
answer: I usually do my homework after I come back from school.

en: I did not understand the last chapter at first.
tamil: கடைசி பாடம் முதல்ல எனக்கு புரியல.
explain: 'Did not' + base verb makes a past negative. 'At first' means in the beginning.
usage: Use it when you tell a teacher where you had trouble.
leelaQ: What was difficult for you at first, but easy later?
answer: Driving was difficult at first, but now it is easy.

en: Did you finish the homework?
tamil: நீ ஹோம்வொர்க்கை முடிச்சிட்டியா?
explain: 'Did' makes a past question. The main verb goes back to the base form.
usage: Use it with classmates before the teacher checks the notebooks.
leelaQ: Do you finish your work on time?
answer: Yes, I try to finish my work before the deadline.

en: She has completed her engineering degree.
tamil: அவ இன்ஜினியரிங் டிகிரியை முடிச்சிருக்கா.
context: Telling someone about a cousin's studies.
explain: 'Has completed' tells about a finished action with a result that matters now.
usage: Use it when you talk about a relative's education in a family chat.
leelaQ: What degree did you study?
answer: I studied commerce at a college in Madurai.

en: The class starts at nine every morning.
tamil: கிளாஸ் தினமும் காலையில ஒன்பது மணிக்கு ஆரம்பிக்கும்.
context: Telling a new student the timing.
explain: Simple present is used for daily routines and fixed timings.
usage: Use it to tell a new student or a parent the class timing.
leelaQ: What time does your class or work start?
answer: My work starts at ten in the morning.

en: Which subject do you find most difficult?
tamil: எந்த பாடம் உனக்கு ரொம்ப கஷ்டமா இருக்கு?
explain: 'Which' is used when you choose from a limited group. 'Find' means think of it as.
usage: Use it to start a study chat with a classmate.
leelaQ: Why is that subject difficult for you?
answer: It is difficult because there are too many formulas.

en: Could you lend me your notes for a day?
tamil: உன் நோட்ஸை ஒரு நாளைக்கு எனக்கு கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
explain: 'Could you' is softer and more polite than 'can you'. 'Lend' means give for a short time.
usage: Use it with a classmate when you missed a class.
leelaQ: Do you lend your things easily to others?
answer: Yes, I lend my notes to my close friends.

en: I am preparing for the NEET exam this year.
tamil: நான் இந்த வருஷம் நீட் தேர்வுக்கு தயாராகிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a relative about your exam plans.
explain: 'Am preparing' shows an effort that is going on for some time, not only right now.
usage: Use it when relatives or neighbours ask what you are doing after school.
leelaQ: What exam are you preparing for?
answer: I am preparing for the bank exam.

en: We submitted the project report yesterday.
tamil: நாங்க நேத்து ப்ராஜெக்ட் ரிப்போர்ட்டை சமர்ப்பிச்சோம்.
context: Telling a friend the project is done.
explain: 'Submitted' is the past form. 'Yesterday' tells the exact time.
usage: Use it with classmates or a guide when asked about your project status.
leelaQ: Have you ever done a college project?
answer: Yes, I made a small billing software for my final year.

en: Have you submitted the assignment yet?
tamil: நீ அசைன்மென்ட்டை இன்னும் சப்மிட் பண்ணலயா?
explain: 'Yet' is used in questions about something expected. 'Have you' begins the question.
usage: Use it when the deadline is near and you want to check with a friend.
leelaQ: When is your next deadline?
answer: My next deadline is on Friday.

en: Revising a little every day works better than studying all night.
tamil: ஒவ்வொரு நாளும் கொஞ்சம் கொஞ்சமா திருப்பி படிக்கிறது ராத்திரி முழுக்க படிக்கிறதை விட நல்லா வேலை செய்யும்.
context: Giving a study tip to a junior.
explain: 'Revising' works as the subject. 'Better than' compares two study methods.
usage: Use it when you advise a younger student about exam preparation.
leelaQ: What is your best study tip?
answer: My best tip is to revise a little every day.

en: Don't copy from your friend's answer sheet.
tamil: உன் நண்பனோட விடைத்தாள்ல இருந்து காப்பி அடிக்காத.
explain: 'Don't' + verb is a negative command. Copying in an exam is wrong.
usage: Use it as advice with a younger sibling or a friend during an exam.
leelaQ: Why is honesty important in exams?
answer: Honesty is important because marks should show real effort.

en: Please explain the last point once more, madam.
tamil: மேடம், கடைசி பாயிண்டை இன்னொரு தடவை விளக்குங்க, தயவுசெஞ்சு.
explain: Adding 'madam' or 'sir' shows respect. 'Once more' asks for a repeat.
usage: Use it with a teacher when you do not follow something in class.
leelaQ: How do you ask a teacher for help?
answer: I raise my hand and ask politely.

en: I should practise English speaking daily.
tamil: நான் தினமும் இங்கிலீஷ் பேசி பழகணும்.
context: Telling yourself or a friend about a goal.
explain: 'Should' gives advice or a duty. Note: the verb is 'practise' in British spelling.
usage: Use it when you talk about your learning goals with a friend or teacher.
leelaQ: How do you practise your English every day?
answer: I speak with my friends and watch English videos.

en: Which college are you planning to join?
tamil: நீ எந்த காலேஜ்ல சேரப் போற?
explain: 'Planning to' + verb talks about a plan. 'Which' offers a choice.
usage: Use it with a school leaver or their parents after the results.
leelaQ: What kind of college would you like to join?
answer: I would like a college with good teachers.

en: My brother is joining a college in Coimbatore next month.
tamil: என் தம்பி அடுத்த மாசம் கோயம்புத்தூர்ல ஒரு காலேஜ்ல சேரப் போறான்.
context: Sharing family news with a neighbour.
explain: 'Is joining' with 'next month' talks about a fixed plan in the near future.
usage: Use it with neighbours or colleagues when you share a family update.
leelaQ: Which college or school did you go to?
answer: I went to a government school near my house.

en: The professor gave us a new assignment today.
tamil: ப்ரொபசர் இன்னைக்கு எங்களுக்கு புது அசைன்மென்ட் கொடுத்தாரு.
context: Telling a roommate about college work.
explain: 'Gave' is the past of give. 'Us' is the person who receives.
usage: Use it with hostel mates or friends when you complain about workload.
leelaQ: Do you like getting assignments?
answer: Not really, but they help me learn the topic well.

en: Will the teacher give us extra time?
tamil: டீச்சர் நமக்கு கூடுதல் நேரம் தருவாங்களா?
context: Asking a classmate in the exam hall.
explain: 'Will' starts a question about the future. 'Extra time' means more than the fixed time.
usage: Use it with classmates when a test looks too long.
leelaQ: What do you do when you run out of time?
answer: I write the short answers first and then the long ones.

en: I have already revised the first three chapters.
tamil: நான் முதல் மூணு பாடத்தை ஏற்கனவே திருப்பி படிச்சிட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about your progress.
explain: 'Already' goes between 'have' and the main verb. It shows the work is done earlier than expected.
usage: Use it when a friend asks how far your exam preparation has gone.
leelaQ: How much of your work have you finished today?
answer: I have finished half of my work today.

en: Sit down quietly and complete the exercise.
tamil: அமைதியா உட்கார்ந்து பயிற்சியை முடிங்க.
explain: Two commands are joined by 'and'. 'Quietly' tells how to sit.
usage: Use it as a teacher or a tutor with a group of children.
leelaQ: What helps you stay calm in class?
answer: Sitting near the front helps me stay calm.

en: Our school reopens after the summer holidays on Monday.
tamil: கோடை விடுமுறைக்கு அப்புறம் எங்க ஸ்கூல் திங்கள்கிழமை திறக்கும்.
context: Telling a parent the reopening day.
explain: Simple present is used for official schedules, like school dates.
usage: Use it with parents or neighbours when they ask about the school calendar.
leelaQ: What do you do during the summer holidays?
answer: I visit my grandparents in my native village.

en: I have not started my project yet.
tamil: நான் இன்னும் என் ப்ராஜெக்ட்டை ஆரம்பிக்கவே இல்ல.
explain: 'Have not ... yet' means something is still undone. It is common in spoken English.
usage: Use it when someone asks about the progress of your work.
leelaQ: What task do you want to start today?
answer: I want to start my English practice today.

en: How many chapters are there in the syllabus?
tamil: சிலபஸ்ல எத்தனை பாடங்கள் இருக்கு?
explain: 'How many' is for countable things. 'There are' shows the existence.
usage: Use it when you plan your time with a friend or a teacher.
leelaQ: How many hours do you need for each chapter?
answer: I need about two hours for one chapter.

en: I will ask my teacher about this doubt tomorrow.
tamil: இந்த சந்தேகத்தை நாளைக்கு என் டீச்சர்கிட்ட கேப்பேன்.
context: Telling a classmate you will clear a doubt.
explain: 'Doubt' in Indian English means a question about a lesson. 'Will ask' shows a plan.
usage: Use it with classmates when neither of you can solve a problem.
leelaQ: What do you do when you have a doubt in a lesson?
answer: I ask my teacher or search on the internet.

en: Group study helps me understand difficult topics.
tamil: குரூப் ஸ்டடி கஷ்டமான டாபிக்குகளை புரிஞ்சுக்க எனக்கு உதவுது.
context: Explaining why you study with friends.
explain: 'Helps me understand' is a common pattern: help + person + verb.
usage: Use it when someone asks why you study with friends.
leelaQ: Do you like studying alone or with friends?
answer: I like studying with friends because we share ideas.

en: Are you studying for the test tonight?
tamil: நீ இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி டெஸ்டுக்கு படிக்கப் போறியா?
explain: 'Are you studying' with 'tonight' asks about a plan for the near future.
usage: Use it with a roommate when you want to study together.
leelaQ: What time do you usually go to bed during exams?
answer: I go to bed around eleven during exams.

en: Could you please send me the assignment details?
tamil: அசைன்மென்ட் விவரங்களை எனக்கு அனுப்ப முடியுமா, தயவுசெஞ்சு?
context: Messaging a classmate or a teacher.
explain: 'Could you please' is very polite. Good for emails and messages.
usage: Use it in a message to a teacher or a friend who has the information.
leelaQ: How do you share notes with your friends?
answer: We share them in a WhatsApp group.

en: He scored ninety percent in the maths test.
tamil: அவன் கணக்கு டெஸ்ட்ல தொண்ணூறு சதவீதம் வாங்கினான்.
context: Telling parents about a friend's marks.
explain: 'Scored' is used for marks or points. 'Percent' needs a number before it.
usage: Use it when you talk about a classmate's or a child's result.
leelaQ: What was your best score in school?
answer: I got ninety five in my science exam.

en: The practical exam is going to be tough this time.
tamil: இந்த தடவை ப்ராக்டிகல் எக்ஸாம் கஷ்டமா இருக்கப் போகுது.
context: Warning a friend before an exam.
explain: 'Is going to be' is used when you expect something from what you already know.
usage: Use it with batch mates when the lab exam is near.
leelaQ: Which is tougher for you, theory or practical?
answer: Theory is tougher for me because there is too much to read.

en: What is the easiest way to improve my spoken English?
tamil: என் பேச்சு இங்கிலீஷை மேம்படுத்த சுலபமான வழி என்ன?
explain: 'The best way to + verb' is a useful pattern to ask for advice.
usage: Use it with a teacher or a friend who speaks good English.
leelaQ: What do you do every day to improve your English?
answer: I speak for ten minutes with my friend every day.

en: I am learning Angular from online videos.
tamil: நான் ஆன்லைன் வீடியோக்கள்ல இருந்து ஆங்குலர் கத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a colleague how you study a new skill.
explain: 'From' shows the source of learning. 'Am learning' shows a task still in progress.
usage: Use it in an office chat when you talk about upskilling yourself.
leelaQ: What new skill are you learning now?
answer: I am learning to code in Angular.

en: We don't have any class tomorrow.
tamil: நமக்கு நாளைக்கு கிளாஸ் எதுவும் இல்ல.
explain: 'Don't have any' means none. Simple present is used for a fixed schedule.
usage: Use it when a holiday is announced or a teacher is absent.
leelaQ: What will you do if you have a free day?
answer: I will sleep late and meet my friends.

en: Please submit your records by Friday.
tamil: உங்க ரெக்கார்டு நோட்டை வெள்ளிக்கிழமைக்குள்ள சமர்ப்பிங்க.
context: A lab teacher giving a deadline.
explain: 'By Friday' means on or before Friday. 'Records' are lab notebooks.
usage: Teachers use it to give clear deadlines to a class.
leelaQ: Do you always meet your deadlines?
answer: Yes, I always try to finish before the last day.

en: We must finish the syllabus before the model exams.
tamil: மாடல் எக்ஸாமுக்கு முன்னாடி நாம சிலபஸை முடிச்சே ஆகணும்.
context: A teacher or leader reminding the class.
explain: 'Must' shows a strong duty. 'Before' sets the deadline.
usage: Use it when you remind classmates or students about a deadline.
leelaQ: How do you plan to complete your syllabus on time?
answer: I divide the chapters and finish a few each day.

en: Who is taking the class after lunch?
tamil: லஞ்சுக்கு அப்புறம் யாரு கிளாஸ் எடுக்கப் போறாங்க?
context: Asking a classmate about the timetable.
explain: 'Who' is the subject here, so no 'do' or 'does' is needed.
usage: Use it in school or college to know the next teacher.
leelaQ: Which period do you like the most?
answer: I like the computer period the most.

en: She has been selected for the science exhibition.
tamil: அவ சயின்ஸ் எக்ஸிபிஷனுக்கு தேர்வு செய்யப்பட்டிருக்கா.
context: Sharing good news about a student.
explain: 'Has been selected' is passive: the action happens to her. The result is true now.
usage: Use it to share a classmate's or a daughter's good news.
leelaQ: Have you ever won a prize in school?
answer: Yes, I won a prize in a drawing competition.

en: I made a study timetable for the whole week.
tamil: நான் முழு வாரத்துக்கும் ஒரு படிப்பு டைம் டேபிள் போட்டேன்.
explain: 'Made a timetable' is the usual collocation. 'The whole week' means all seven days.
usage: Use it when you share your study plan with a friend or a parent.
leelaQ: Do you follow a timetable every day?
answer: Yes, I follow it, but sometimes I change the timings.

en: Do we have homework for tomorrow?
tamil: நமக்கு நாளைக்கு ஹோம்வொர்க் இருக்கா?
explain: 'Do we have' asks if something exists. It is very common among students.
usage: Use it with a classmate when you missed the teacher's instruction.
leelaQ: What homework is the hardest for you?
answer: Writing long essays is the hardest for me.

en: The library is quiet, so I study there.
tamil: லைப்ரரி அமைதியா இருக்கு, அதனால நான் அங்க படிக்கிறேன்.
context: Explaining where you prefer to study.
explain: 'So' gives the result of the reason before it. Simple present shows a habit.
usage: Use it when someone asks why you go to the library.
leelaQ: Where do you like to study or work?
answer: I like to work at a table near the window.

en: Please read the instructions carefully before you start.
tamil: தொடங்குறதுக்கு முன்னாடி வழிமுறைகளை கவனமா படிங்க.
explain: 'Before you start' gives the order of the actions. 'Carefully' is an adverb.
usage: Invigilators and teachers say it before tests begin.
leelaQ: Why is it important to read instructions?
answer: It is important because wrong steps give wrong answers.

en: Our final year project is about a billing software.
tamil: எங்க ஃபைனல் இயர் ப்ராஜெக்ட் ஒரு பில்லிங் சாஃப்ட்வேர் பத்தினது.
context: Telling an interviewer about your project.
explain: 'Is about' tells the topic of something. Useful in interviews.
usage: Use it in a job interview or a college viva when asked about your project.
leelaQ: Can you tell me about your project?
answer: My project is a billing software for small restaurants.

en: Please don't make noise in the library.
tamil: லைப்ரரியில சத்தம் போடாதீங்க, தயவுசெஞ்சு.
explain: 'Please don't' is a polite way to stop an action. 'Make noise' means be loud.
usage: Use it politely with a person who talks loudly where others study.
leelaQ: How do you ask people politely to be quiet?
answer: I say please keep your voice low.

en: How did your interview at the college go?
tamil: காலேஜ்ல உன் இன்டர்வியூ எப்படி போச்சு?
context: Asking a cousin after the interview.
explain: 'How did ... go?' asks about the result of an event. 'Go' is in base form after 'did'.
usage: Use it with a friend or relative who has just faced an interview.
leelaQ: How do you prepare for an interview?
answer: I practise common questions in front of a mirror.

en: I will take notes during the lecture.
tamil: நான் லெக்சர் நேரத்துல நோட்ஸ் எடுப்பேன்.
context: Telling a friend who missed class.
explain: 'During' is followed by an event. 'Take notes' means write the key points.
usage: Use it when a friend asks you to help with class notes.
leelaQ: Do you write notes in class?
answer: Yes, I write short points in my notebook.

en: The teacher is checking our answer papers now.
tamil: டீச்சர் இப்போ நம்ம விடைத்தாள்களை திருத்திட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Telling a friend waiting for results.
explain: 'Is checking' shows the action is happening at this moment.
usage: Use it with classmates when everyone is waiting for marks.
leelaQ: How do you feel while waiting for results?
answer: I feel nervous, but I try to stay calm.

en: Can you explain this sum to me once more?
tamil: இந்த கணக்கை இன்னொரு தடவை எனக்கு விளக்க முடியுமா?
explain: 'Can you ...?' is a polite way to ask for help. 'Once more' means one more time.
usage: Use it with a friend or a teacher when you did not follow a step.
leelaQ: Who explains things best to you?
answer: My elder brother explains things best to me.

en: Can I sit next to you in the class?
tamil: நான் கிளாஸ்ல உன் பக்கத்துல உட்காரலாமா?
explain: 'Can I' asks for permission. 'Next to' means beside.
usage: Use it on your first day in a new class or college.
leelaQ: Where do you like to sit in a class?
answer: I like to sit in the middle so I can see and hear well.

en: My daughter goes to tuition after school.
tamil: என் பொண்ணு ஸ்கூல் முடிஞ்சு டியூஷனுக்கு போறா.
context: A parent chatting with another parent.
explain: 'Tuition' means private lessons in India. 'Goes' has -es because of 'she'.
usage: Use it with other parents when you talk about your child's routine.
leelaQ: Do children need tuition after school?
answer: Some do, but good teaching in school is enough for many.

en: I have understood this topic now, thank you.
tamil: எனக்கு இப்போ இந்த டாபிக் புரிஞ்சிடுச்சு, நன்றி.
context: Thanking a teacher after an explanation.
explain: 'Have understood' shows the result is clear now. 'Thank you' makes it polite.
usage: Use it with a teacher or friend after they explain a difficult point.
leelaQ: What was the last difficult thing you understood?
answer: I understood how bank interest is calculated.

en: Where can I get the previous year question papers?
tamil: முந்தைய வருஷ கேள்வித்தாள்கள் எங்க கிடைக்கும்?
explain: 'Where can I get' asks for a place or source. 'Previous year' means last year.
usage: Use it with seniors or the librarian before an exam.
leelaQ: Where do you usually find study material?
answer: I find it on the college website and in the library.

en: Writing the answers by hand helps me remember them.
tamil: விடைகளை கையால எழுதினா அது எனக்கு நினைவுல இருக்கும்.
explain: 'Writing' is a gerund used as the subject of the sentence.
usage: Use it when you discuss study methods with friends.
leelaQ: How do you remember new words?
answer: I write them in a notebook and use them in sentences.

en: I can't concentrate when the TV is on.
tamil: டிவி ஓடிட்டு இருக்கும்போது என்னால கவனம் செலுத்த முடியாது.
explain: 'Can't' shows inability. 'When' joins the problem with its cause.
usage: Use it at home when you need quiet for your studies.
leelaQ: What helps you concentrate on your work?
answer: A quiet room and a cup of tea help me.

en: Please give me a little more time to finish this.
tamil: இதை முடிக்க எனக்கு இன்னும் கொஞ்சம் நேரம் கொடுங்க.
context: Asking a teacher during a test.
explain: 'A little more' softens the request. 'To finish' gives the reason.
usage: Use it with a teacher or a lecturer when you are almost done.
leelaQ: What do you do when you need more time?
answer: I politely ask my manager for a short extension.

en: The seminar was very useful for all the students.
tamil: அந்த செமினார் எல்லா மாணவர்களுக்கும் ரொம்ப பயனுள்ளதா இருந்துச்சு.
explain: 'Was' links the seminar with the description. 'Useful for' shows who benefits.
usage: Use it in feedback forms or when you speak to a principal about an event.
leelaQ: Did you attend any useful programme recently?
answer: Yes, I attended a workshop on time management.

en: Have you prepared for the viva?
tamil: நீ வைவாவுக்கு தயாராகிட்டியா?
explain: 'Viva' is an oral exam. 'Have you prepared' checks the present state of readiness.
usage: Use it with lab partners before the oral exam.
leelaQ: Do you feel confident about speaking in an exam?
answer: I feel a little nervous, but I know my subject.

en: I am going to apply for a scholarship this year.
tamil: நான் இந்த வருஷம் ஒரு ஸ்காலர்ஷிப்புக்கு விண்ணப்பிக்கப் போறேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a plan.
explain: 'Am going to' shows a plan already decided.
usage: Use it with friends or teachers when you talk about funds for studies.
leelaQ: What are your plans for higher studies?
answer: I want to do a master's degree after my graduation.

en: Last week I attended a workshop on public speaking.
tamil: போன வாரம் நான் பொது பேச்சு பத்தின ஒரு வொர்க்ஷாப்புக்கு போனேன்.
explain: 'Last week' sets the time at the start. 'Attended' is used for events.
usage: Use it at the office or in class when you share a training experience.
leelaQ: Are you comfortable speaking in front of people?
answer: Not yet, but I am practising every day.

en: What time will the results be published?
tamil: ரிசல்ட் எத்தனை மணிக்கு வெளியிடுவாங்க?
context: Asking an office or a friend.
explain: 'Will be published' is passive future. 'What time' asks for the clock time.
usage: Use it on result day when you check with a friend or a clerk.
leelaQ: What will you do after you see your results?
answer: I will call my parents first.

en: You can learn almost anything from YouTube these days.
tamil: இப்போல்லாம் யூடியூப்ல இருந்து கிட்டத்தட்ட எல்லாத்தையும் கத்துக்கலாம்.
explain: 'Can' shows it is possible. 'Almost' means nearly.
usage: Use it when you encourage a friend who cannot afford coaching.
leelaQ: What did you learn from the internet recently?
answer: I learned how to make a simple website.

en: Could you recommend a good book for learning grammar?
tamil: இலக்கணம் கத்துக்க ஒரு நல்ல புத்தகத்தை பரிந்துரைக்க முடியுமா?
explain: 'Recommend' means suggest something good. 'Could you' is polite.
usage: Use it with an English teacher or a friend who studies well.
leelaQ: What book are you reading these days?
answer: I am reading a short story book in English.

en: The results will come out next Friday.
tamil: ரிசல்ட் அடுத்த வெள்ளிக்கிழமை வரும்.
explain: 'Come out' means to be published. 'Will' is used for a known future fact.
usage: Use it when a student or a parent asks when the marks will arrive.
leelaQ: How do you feel before the results come?
answer: I feel a little scared, but I hope for the best.

en: He will not join the tuition next year.
tamil: அவன் அடுத்த வருஷம் டியூஷன்ல சேர மாட்டான்.
context: Telling a neighbour about a decision.
explain: 'Will not' shows a decision or a refusal about the future.
usage: Use it when you talk about a student's decision with other parents.
leelaQ: Do you think tuition is necessary?
answer: Not always, because self-study can also work well.

en: Did you take notes in yesterday's class?
tamil: நேத்து கிளாஸ்ல நீ நோட்ஸ் எடுத்தியா?
explain: 'Yesterday's class' shows the class belongs to yesterday.
usage: Use it when you were absent and need to catch up.
leelaQ: How do you catch up when you miss a class?
answer: I take my friend's notes and read them at home.

en: He is good at maths but weak in English.
tamil: அவன் கணக்குல கெட்டிக்காரன், ஆனா இங்கிலீஷ்ல வீக்.
explain: 'Good at' and 'weak in' are fixed phrases. 'But' shows the contrast.
usage: Use it when you describe a student to a teacher or a parent.
leelaQ: What subject are you good at?
answer: I am good at science and history.

en: I have been studying since six in the morning.
tamil: நான் காலையில ஆறு மணியிலிருந்து படிச்சிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend why you are tired.
explain: 'Have been studying' with 'since' shows an action that started in the past and still continues.
usage: Use it when you explain your tiredness or ask for a break.
leelaQ: How long can you study without a break?
answer: I can study for about one hour without a break.

en: Which topic is the teacher going to cover next?
tamil: டீச்சர் அடுத்து எந்த டாபிக்கை எடுக்கப் போறாங்க?
context: Asking a classmate about the plan.
explain: 'Cover a topic' means to teach it. 'Going to' asks about a plan.
usage: Use it with classmates to read the next lesson in advance.
leelaQ: Do you read the lesson before the class?
answer: Sometimes I do, when I have time.

en: Kindly check my answer sheet once again, sir.
tamil: சார், என் விடைத்தாளை இன்னொரு முறை தயவுசெஞ்சு பாருங்க.
explain: 'Kindly' is a formal and polite word, common in Indian English.
usage: Use it with a lecturer when you think a mark is missing.
leelaQ: How do you ask politely for a second look at something?
answer: I say please check once more, sir.

en: Our college is organising a technical symposium next week.
tamil: எங்க காலேஜ் அடுத்த வாரம் ஒரு டெக்னிக்கல் சிம்போசியம் நடத்துது.
context: Inviting a friend to an event.
explain: 'Is organising' with a future time shows a fixed arrangement.
usage: Use it to invite friends or juniors to a college event.
leelaQ: Do you take part in college events?
answer: Yes, I take part in quiz competitions.

en: I always keep my phone away while studying.
tamil: நான் படிக்கும்போது எப்பவும் என் போனை தள்ளி வச்சிடுவேன்.
explain: 'Always' comes before the main verb. 'While studying' shortens 'while I am studying'.
usage: Use it when you give focus tips to friends or your children.
leelaQ: What distracts you the most when you study?
answer: My phone distracts me the most, so I keep it in another room.

en: How long do you study every day?
tamil: நீ தினமும் எவ்வளவு நேரம் படிப்ப?
explain: 'How long' asks for a length of time. 'Every day' shows habit.
usage: Use it to compare study habits with a friend.
leelaQ: What is a good number of study hours for you?
answer: Four hours a day is good for me.

en: The students are presenting their projects in the hall.
tamil: மாணவர்கள் ஹால்ல தங்களோட ப்ராஜெக்ட்களை சமர்ப்பிச்சிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Telling a visitor what is happening.
explain: 'Are presenting' shows an action in progress. 'Their' belongs to the students.
usage: Use it when you show a guest around a college or a school.
leelaQ: Have you ever presented something in front of a class?
answer: Yes, I once presented my project to the whole class.

en: Never leave your studies for the last minute.
tamil: படிப்பை எப்பவும் கடைசி நிமிஷத்துக்கு விட்டுடாதே.
explain: 'Never' + verb is a strong negative command. 'Last minute' means at the end.
usage: Use it as advice for a junior or your own children.
leelaQ: Do you finish your work early or at the last minute?
answer: I try to finish early, but sometimes I am late.

en: Take a five minute break and then continue studying.
tamil: ஐந்து நிமிஷம் ஓய்வு எடுத்துட்டு அப்புறம் படிப்பை தொடரு.
context: Advising a friend who looks tired.
explain: 'Take a break' is a fixed phrase. 'Then' joins the next action.
usage: Use it with a friend or a child who has studied for long.
leelaQ: What do you do in a short break?
answer: I drink tea and walk for a few minutes.

en: I joined an evening class to improve my spoken English.
tamil: என் பேச்சு இங்கிலீஷை மேம்படுத்த நான் ஒரு ஈவ்னிங் கிளாஸ்ல சேர்ந்தேன்.
context: Telling someone why you started a class.
explain: 'To improve' gives the purpose. 'Spoken English' means speaking skill.
usage: Use it when friends ask why you go out every evening.
leelaQ: Why do you want to improve your English?
answer: I want a better job and more confidence.

en: Is the project deadline this Friday?
tamil: ப்ராஜெக்ட் டெட்லைன் இந்த வெள்ளிக்கிழமையா?
explain: A question with 'is' can be answered with yes or no.
usage: Use it with team members or the guide to avoid confusion.
leelaQ: How do you manage a deadline?
answer: I split the work into small parts and finish one each day.

en: We will have a revision test on Monday.
tamil: எங்களுக்கு திங்கள்கிழமை ஒரு ரிவிஷன் டெஸ்ட் இருக்கு.
explain: 'Will have' is used for planned events. 'On' goes with days.
usage: Use it to remind classmates or children about the next test.
leelaQ: What day is the hardest for you in a week?
answer: Monday is hardest because I wake up late.

en: She teaches maths in a government school.
tamil: அவங்க அரசு பள்ளியில கணக்கு பாடம் எடுக்குறாங்க.
context: Introducing a teacher to a guest.
explain: 'Teaches' takes -es after 'she'. 'In a school' tells the workplace.
usage: Use it when you tell someone about a relative's job.
leelaQ: What does your family do for a living?
answer: My father is a farmer and my mother is a teacher.

en: What did you score in the unit test?
tamil: யூனிட் டெஸ்ட்ல நீ எவ்வளவு மார்க் வாங்கின?
context: Asking a friend after the results.
explain: 'Score' is used for marks. 'Did' makes the past question.
usage: Use it casually with classmates after marks are given.
leelaQ: Are you happy with your marks?
answer: Yes, I am happy because I studied well.

en: Small goals make a big study plan easy to follow.
tamil: சின்ன இலக்குகள் பெரிய படிப்பு திட்டத்தை பின்பற்ற சுலபமாக்கும்.
explain: 'Make something easy' means to cause it to become easy.
usage: Use it when you guide a younger student or a learner.
leelaQ: What small goal can you set for this week?
answer: I will learn five new words every day.

en: Please help me prepare for tomorrow's presentation.
tamil: நாளைய ப்ரசன்டேஷனுக்கு நான் தயாராக உதவுங்க.
context: Asking a friend or a senior.
explain: 'Help me + verb' is a common pattern. 'Tomorrow's' is the possessive form.
usage: Use it with a senior or a friend who is good at speaking.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you have an important task?
answer: My friend helps me with ideas and practice.

en: The headmaster announced the exam dates this morning.
tamil: ஹெட்மாஸ்டர் இன்னைக்கு காலையில தேர்வு தேதிகளை அறிவிச்சாரு.
context: Sharing school news with a parent.
explain: 'Announced' means told everyone officially. 'This morning' is a past time.
usage: Use it with a parent or a friend when the exam schedule is out.
leelaQ: Which exam date worries you the most?
answer: The maths exam worries me the most.

en: I wasn't able to finish the syllabus on time.
tamil: என்னால சிலபஸை நேரத்துக்கு முடிக்க முடியல.
explain: 'Wasn't able to' is a past form of 'can't'. 'On time' means by the correct time.
usage: Use it when you explain to a parent or a teacher why you did not do well.
leelaQ: What stops you from finishing your work on time?
answer: Too many other jobs stop me from finishing.

en: Are you going to attend the extra class on Sunday?
tamil: நீ ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை எக்ஸ்ட்ரா கிளாஸுக்கு வரப் போறியா?
explain: 'Attend' is used for classes and events. 'Going to' asks about the plan.
usage: Use it to check with a friend if they will come for a special class.
leelaQ: How do you spend your Sundays?
answer: I rest, do my laundry, and watch a movie.

en: I will join a coaching centre after my twelfth.
tamil: நான் பன்னிரண்டாம் வகுப்புக்கு அப்புறம் ஒரு கோச்சிங் சென்டர்ல சேருவேன்.
context: Telling a relative your future plan.
explain: 'After my twelfth' is common Indian English for after class 12.
usage: Use it when relatives ask what you plan after school.
leelaQ: What will you do after your studies?
answer: I will look for a job in a software company.

en: Our lab assistant showed us how to use the microscope.
tamil: எங்க லேப் அசிஸ்டென்ட் மைக்ரோஸ்கோப்பை எப்படி பயன்படுத்தணும்னு காட்டினாரு.
explain: 'Showed us how to + verb' explains a demonstration.
usage: Use it when you tell a parent about what you did in the lab.
leelaQ: What was the most interesting class you ever had?
answer: The most interesting class was a science experiment.

en: Do you prefer studying alone or in a group?
tamil: நீ தனியா படிக்கிறதை விரும்புவியா இல்ல குரூப்பாவா?
explain: 'Prefer' is followed by -ing. 'Or' gives two choices.
usage: Use it with new friends to learn about their study style.
leelaQ: Why do you prefer that way?
answer: I prefer it because I can focus better.

en: Let us make a study plan for this month.
tamil: இந்த மாசத்துக்கு ஒரு படிப்பு திட்டம் போடலாம்.
explain: 'Let us' invites someone to do something together.
usage: Use it with a friend or a sibling to start planning together.
leelaQ: What is one thing you want to finish this month?
answer: I want to finish a small online course this month.

en: I am doing my MBA through distance education.
tamil: நான் தொலைதூர கல்வி மூலமா என் எம்பிஏ படிச்சிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
explain: 'Through' shows the method. 'Am doing' shows a longer ongoing task.
usage: Use it with colleagues when you work and study together.
leelaQ: Do you want to study more while working?
answer: Yes, I want to do a course on weekends.

en: I have booked my seat for the entrance exam.
tamil: நான் நுழைவுத் தேர்வுக்கு என் இடத்தை பதிவு பண்ணிட்டேன்.
explain: 'Have booked' shows the work is done and ready now. 'Entrance exam' tests you to enter a college.
usage: Use it when your friends ask about the exam registration.
leelaQ: Have you registered for any exam recently?
answer: Yes, I registered for a typing test last month.

en: Why are you learning Angular?
tamil: நீ ஏன் ஆங்குலர் கத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்க?
context: A friend asks about your new skill.
explain: 'Why' asks for a reason. Answer with 'because' or 'to'.
usage: Use it with a colleague or a friend who is starting a new course.
leelaQ: What do you want to build with it?
answer: I want to build a small app for practising English.

en: Every Saturday, we have a small quiz in class.
tamil: ஒவ்வொரு சனிக்கிழமையும் நாங்க கிளாஸ்ல ஒரு சின்ன க்விஸ் வைப்போம்.
explain: 'Every Saturday' at the start shows a regular habit.
usage: Use it to explain your weekly class routine to a new friend.
leelaQ: Do you enjoy quizzes?
answer: Yes, I enjoy them because they make learning fun.

en: There is no need to panic before the exam.
tamil: பரீட்சைக்கு முன்னாடி பயப்பட வேண்டிய அவசியம் இல்ல.
explain: 'There is no need to + verb' means it is not necessary. It sounds calm and kind.
usage: Use it to calm a nervous friend or a child before a test.
leelaQ: How do you stay calm before a big day?
answer: I take deep breaths and do a short walk.

en: Could you share the link for the online class?
tamil: ஆன்லைன் கிளாஸுக்கான லிங்கை பகிர முடியுமா?
context: Messaging a teacher or a group.
explain: 'Share the link' is a normal phrase for online classes.
usage: Use it in a class group chat when you cannot find the class link.
leelaQ: Do you prefer online classes or classroom classes?
answer: I prefer classroom classes because I can ask questions easily.

en: My friend helped me with the maths problems.
tamil: என் நண்பன் கணக்கு பிரச்சனைகள்ல எனக்கு உதவி பண்ணான்.
explain: 'Helped me with' is followed by a thing. 'Problems' here means sums.
usage: Use it when someone asks how you solved a tough sum.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you are stuck?
answer: My elder sister helps me when I am stuck.

en: Have you chosen a topic for your presentation?
tamil: உன் ப்ரசன்டேஷனுக்கு ஒரு தலைப்பு தேர்ந்தெடுத்துட்டியா?
explain: 'Have you chosen' asks about a decision already made.
usage: Use it with a classmate before a seminar.
leelaQ: What topic would you like to talk about?
answer: I would like to talk about my favourite cricketer.

en: Reading the question paper carefully saves a lot of mistakes.
tamil: கேள்வித்தாளை கவனமா படிக்கிறது நிறைய தவறுகளை தவிர்க்கும்.
explain: 'Carefully' tells how to read. 'Saves mistakes' means avoids them.
usage: Use it when you advise juniors or your children before an exam.
leelaQ: What do you do first when you get a question paper?
answer: I read all the questions once before I start.
